_README: Durable notes surfaced in the Fix queue tab of reports/site-report.html.
The report is regenerated in full every run, so notes MUST live here — anything typed into the HTML is lost on the next run.
Keys are scraper names exactly as they appear in scrapers/scraper-registry.js, plus the special key _global.
Each value: { note: string, priority: 'high'|'normal'|'low', added: 'YYYY-MM-DD' }.
A note on a scraper with no detected issues still shows up in the Fix queue, so this doubles as a to-do list.

_global.note: Before fixing anything, read SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl for whether the scraper is already diagnosed or known-dead. Verify a claim before acting on it — do not archive a scraper as 'covered elsewhere' without confirming the replacement returns real events for that specific site. Run `node -c <file>` on every modified scraper, and append one line per logical fix to SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl.

WordPress-GA.note: Part of the known WordPress-{state} platform-heterogeneity problem: each library runs a different theme/plugin, so there is no generic patch — this needs per-site DOM work. Confirm against the live page before changing selectors.

WordPress-TN.note: Step 3d found URL collisions in this family on 2026-08-04 (Seymour TN resolving to CT, Baxter TN to ME, and three separate states pointing at spartalibrary.org). Treat as a seed-data bug — fix the per-site URLs in the config array, do not touch extraction code.
